verdict.headline: Marvell beats but sinks premarket, narrowing AI trade to Nvidia ahead of Warsh debut
verdict.horizon: Through Warsh keynote 10 AM ET today; reassess for Friday afternoon session
verdict.rationale_short: Marvell's Q2 beat — revenue $2.74B (vs $2.72B est), adj. EPS $0.94 (vs $0.93 est) — was real but razor-thin after a 187% YTD run, and the Q3 guide of $3.15B was undercut by gross margin compression concerns, sending shares -7.58% premarket. Rubrik's parallel -8.30% premarket (after surging +11.33% in Thursday's regular session on its own beat) reinforces the pattern: the bar for high-multiple tech infrastructure is priced for perfection, and anything short of a blowout sells. The AMD divergence — down 0.91% Thursday while NVDA gained 8.74% — has now been extended into Friday's premarket via MRVL: the market's answer is emphatically that AI demand is Blackwell-specific, not a broad-based semi cycle. Nasdaq futures -0.32% vs S&P -0.04% maps that story precisely. Warsh's 10 AM ET Jackson Hole keynote is the week's defining event: with September hike odds at ~33%, 10Y at 4.66% (+2bps), and headline PCE at 3.7% alongside a softening labor market, the asymmetry is live in both directions. A dovish framing pushes the rate-regime risk formally off the table; a hawkish framing citing Canada tariff cost-push re-activates compression concerns heading into September FOMC. Hold positions; add nothing new ahead of the podium.

trade_setups.asset: MRVL — post-earnings mean reversion vs. structural support
trade_setups.thesis: MRVL's -7.58% premarket on a narrow beat after a 187% YTD run is a valuation-compression event, not a thesis-destruction event. The Google custom chip deal ($12.2B) and AI data-infrastructure exposure remain structurally intact. The market is repricing gross margin risk — when that recalibration completes, the setup shifts to whether the August 1 earnings base (~$88-90) holds as support. At current pre-market prices (~$97), the stock is offering the first meaningful risk-adjusted entry since the May breakout.
trade_setups.entry: A stabilization pattern on above-average volume after the initial gap down — ideally a hammer or doji on the 30-minute chart near $94-97 — would be the entry signal. A close below the August 1 earnings base ($88) would invalidate and signal a deeper recalibration toward the July gap fill at $82.
trade_setups.invalidation: Warsh hawkish keynote raising the 30Y above 5.25% adds rate-compression to the margin-compression already in play; that combination would extend the selloff below $88. Also invalidated if MRVL management comments on the earnings call (if any) confirm the margin issue is structural rather than transient.

trade_setups.asset: Warsh keynote asymmetry — rates and risk assets
trade_setups.thesis: September hike odds at 33% mean Warsh's 10 AM ET speech is the most asymmetric market event since May's inaugural FOMC. Inflation at 3.4% (core PCE) and labor softening are the two signal variables — the Chair who dwells on inflation is hawkish, the Chair who dwells on jobs is dovish. The backdrop is arguably the most constructive since late 2025: NVDA confirmed AI capex, durable goods +1.1%, MRVL/RBRK selloffs are valuation not demand. A dovish framing formally deactivates the 30Y regime trigger (currently at 5.16%, trigger 5.30%) for the first time since mid-July.
trade_setups.entry: 30Y remaining below 5.20% through Friday close (confirmed dovish) would be the regime-deactivation signal; add risk exposure into the September 16 FOMC window. A 10Y spike through 4.75% on a hawkish surprise would be the stop signal for any risk longs added this week.
trade_setups.invalidation: Oil spike toward $89-91 on any Bessent sanction named before Warsh speaks would hand the Fed Chair a simultaneous commodity-inflation signal that increases the probability of a hawkish framing regardless of his prepared remarks.
trade_setups.horizon: 10 AM ET today through September 16 FOMC.

trade_setups.asset: NVDA vs. sector — long NVDA, reduce AMD/MRVL weight
trade_setups.thesis: The divergence is now confirmed across three data points: AMD -0.91% Thursday despite NVDA +8.74%, MRVL -7.58% Friday despite a beat, and RBRK -8.30% in a parallel 'sell the news'. NVDA at $227.98 is the sole institutional conviction trade in the AI semi complex. The pair trade — long NVDA, light on AMD/MRVL — captures both the confirmed demand cycle and the mean-reversion risk in the crowded names.
trade_setups.entry: NVDA already confirmed above $220 (closed $227.98). The pair trade entry is already live for those who followed Wednesday's setup. Trimming AMD below $470 on continued divergence and MRVL at open-price stabilization would complete the rotation.
trade_setups.invalidation: Warsh dovish framing triggers a sector-wide relief rally that lifts AMD through $484 and MRVL back above $105 — in that scenario, the narrow-NVDA thesis dilutes and the pair trade should be unwound.

bear_case: MRVL's -7.58% on a beat that beat by $0.01 EPS and $20M revenue is the most concentrated signal the tape has delivered this week: the AI infrastructure trade outside Blackwell is a valuation problem, not just a timing problem. If NVDA at $227.98 is 24x+ forward revenue, MRVL at $97 after a 187% YTD run and a narrow beat carries the same risk. The same 'sell the news' dynamic that hit RBRK (-9.73% AH despite beating rev by $31M) applies everywhere the setup was already priced for perfection. Warsh's hawkish framing — citing 3.7% headline PCE, Canada tariff cost-push effective September 8, and a labor market that hasn't broken decisively — would push the 10Y through 4.75% and re-rate the entire high-multiple complex simultaneously with the sector's worst post-earnings print of the cycle. The 30Y at 5.16% is 14bps from a formal regime trigger; a hawkish keynote puts it there before the September 16 FOMC. In that scenario, the NVDA beat becomes a ceiling not a floor — priced for perfection at a moment when the rate backdrop is re-tightening.
